question: According to the Census of India 2011, ‘Other Religions and Persuasions (ORP)’ comprise how much of the population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.9 million.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, persons following ‘Other Religions and Persuasions (ORP)’ — tribal/animist faiths not classified under the six major religions — numbered about 79,99,378, i.e. roughly 7.9 million (0.65% of the population). (जनगणना 2011, अन्य धर्म एवं संप्रदाय — 7.9 मिलियन)

 

• The Census of India 2011 recorded six major religions separately — Hindu (79.8%), Muslim (14.2%), Christian (2.3%), Sikh (1.7%), Buddhist (0.7%) and Jain (0.4%) — with the residual category grouped as ‘Other Religions and Persuasions’ and a small share as ‘Religion Not Stated’ (0.24%).

 

• ORP mainly comprises indigenous/tribal faiths such as those practised by various Scheduled Tribes across India, which do not fall under any of the six major recognised religions.

 

• The 2011 Census was conducted under the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (RGI), Ministry of Home Affairs, and its religion data was released in 2015.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2011 Census was India's 15th Census and the 7th after Independence; the next Census is due to be conducted after 2011.

 

• Among major religions, the Muslim population recorded the highest decadal growth rate (2001-2011), while the Hindu population's share declined marginally compared to 2001.

 

NOTE

 

• 3.9 million (Option 1): This understates the actual ORP figure recorded in Census 2011.

 

• 5.9 million (Option 3): This also understates the actual ORP figure recorded in Census 2011.

 

• 9.9 million (Option 4): This overstates the actual ORP figure recorded in Census 2011.

question: When was the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award renamed as Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6th August 2021.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Government of India renamed the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award as the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award on 6th August 2021, announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. (मेजर ध्यानचंद खेल रत्न पुरस्कार — 6 अगस्त 2021)

 

• The award was renamed in honour of Major Dhyan Chand, the legendary hockey player known as the ‘Wizard of Hockey’, whose birthday (29 August) is celebrated as National Sports Day in India.

 

• The Khel Ratna Award is India's highest sporting honour, given for the most spectacular and outstanding performance in the field of sports over a period of four years.

 

• The renaming was announced just after the conclusion of the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games (held in 2021), amid a wave of national tributes to Indian sporting achievements.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's other major sports honours include the Arjuna Award, Dronacharya Award (for coaches) and Dhyan Chand Award (for lifetime achievement, itself later renamed to avoid duplication after the Khel Ratna renaming).

 

• Neeraj Chopra was among the prominent recipients of the (newly renamed) Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award following his gold medal at the Tokyo Olympics.

 

NOTE

 

• 6th August 2022 (Option 1): Incorrect year — the renaming took place in 2021, not 2022.

 

• 5th January 2022 (Option 2): Incorrect date and year.

 

• 5th January 2021 (Option 4): Incorrect date; the actual announcement was made on 6th August 2021.

question: Who among the following was appointed as the Governor of Jharkhand in February 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is CP Radhakrishnan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• C.P. Radhakrishnan, a senior BJP leader from Tamil Nadu, was appointed as the Governor of Jharkhand in February 2023, succeeding Ramesh Bais, who was transferred to Maharashtra. (सी.पी. राधाकृष्णन — झारखंड के राज्यपाल, फरवरी 2023)

 

• He had earlier served as the Governor of Telangana (additional charge) and was later, in July 2024, moved to become Governor of Maharashtra.

 

• C.P. Radhakrishnan went on to be elected as the 15th President of India in 2025, succeeding President Droupadi Murmu.

 

• The Governor of a State is appointed by the President of India under Article 155 of the Constitution, and holds office during the pleasure of the President.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jharkhand's Chief Minister at the time of this appointment (2023) was Hemant Soren of the JMM.

 

• State Governors are typically rotated across states; Ramesh Bais himself had earlier served as Governor of Tripura before Jharkhand.

 

NOTE

 

• Ramesh Bais (Option 2): He was the outgoing Governor of Jharkhand, transferred to Maharashtra in February 2023 — he was replaced, not appointed, at this time.

 

• T Gahlot (Option 3): Not appointed Governor of Jharkhand in February 2023.

 

• RN Ravi (Option 4): He was appointed Governor of Tamil Nadu in September 2021, not Jharkhand.

question: Where was the first women’s international test cricket match hosted in India in 1976?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bangalore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's first women's international Test cricket match on home soil was played at Bangalore (Bengaluru) against West Indies, from 31 October to 2 November 1976. (महिला टेस्ट क्रिकेट — बैंगलोर, 1976)

 

• This match was part of the West Indies women's cricket team's tour of India in 1976-77, India's first home Test series in women's cricket.

 

• This Bangalore Test was, in fact, India's very first women's Test match ever — India's national women's team made its international Test debut in this same match against West Indies.

 

• The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) took over administration of women's cricket in India only in 2006; before that it was governed by the Women's Cricket Association of India (WCAI).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 1976-77 series against West Indies also featured Tests at Pune, Jamshedpur, Patna and Delhi, but the opening/first Test was at Bangalore.

 

• Shantha Rangaswamy was among the pioneering captains of the early Indian women's Test team in this era.

 

NOTE

 

• New Delhi (Option 1): Delhi hosted one of the later Tests in the 1976-77 series, not the first one.

 

• Mumbai (Option 3): Mumbai was not the venue of the first women's home Test in 1976.

 

• Kolkata (Option 4): Kolkata was not the venue of the first women's home Test in 1976.

question: Who among the following founded the Atmiya Sabha in 1814?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raja Rammohun Roy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raja Rammohun Roy founded the Atmiya Sabha in Calcutta in 1814, a forerunner of the later Brahmo Samaj, to discuss and propagate monotheistic ideas and social reform. (आत्मीय सभा — राजा राममोहन राय)

 

• The Atmiya Sabha campaigned against practices such as sati, polygamy, child marriage and idol worship, and promoted rational, Vedanta-based monotheism.

 

• Rammohun Roy later founded the Brahmo Sabha in 1828, which evolved into the Brahmo Samaj, one of the most influential socio-religious reform movements of 19th-century Bengal.

 

• He is widely regarded as the ‘Father of the Indian Renaissance’ and played a key role in the abolition of Sati through Governor-General Lord William Bentinck's Regulation XVII of 1829.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Debendranath Tagore later reorganised the Brahmo Samaj and founded the Tattwabodhini Sabha in 1839.

 

• Keshab Chandra Sen later led a faction that split to form the Brahmo Samaj of India in 1866.

 

NOTE

 

• Keshab Chandra Sen (Option 1): He joined and later led a faction of the Brahmo Samaj decades after its founding; he did not found the Atmiya Sabha.

 

• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar (Option 3): He was a reformer known for work on widow remarriage and Bengali education, not the founder of Atmiya Sabha.

 

• Debendranath Tagore (Option 4): He reorganised and strengthened the Brahmo Samaj after Rammohun Roy, but did not found the Atmiya Sabha.

question: Kajari Mahotsav is primarily celebrated in which of the following districts of Uttar Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mirzapur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kajari Mahotsav is a folk music festival primarily celebrated in Mirzapur district, Uttar Pradesh, centred on the traditional Kajari (Kajri) folk songs sung during the monsoon month of Shravan (Sawan). (कजरी महोत्सव — मिर्जापुर)

 

• Kajari songs are traditionally sung by women, expressing themes of the monsoon, separation of lovers, and devotion, and are especially associated with the Bhojpuri/Awadhi belt of eastern Uttar Pradesh.

 

• The festival is organised by the Uttar Pradesh Department of Tourism/Culture and typically features performances by renowned folk artists, celebrating the region's cultural heritage.

 

• Mirzapur is also historically noted for the Vindhyavasini Devi Temple and its carpet-weaving industry, alongside its association with Kajari folk music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known folk song traditions of Uttar Pradesh include Chaiti, Sohar and Barahmasa, sung during different seasons and life events.

 

• Banaras (Varanasi) is also closely linked with the Kajari singing tradition, alongside Mirzapur.

 

NOTE

 

• Gorakhpur (Option 2): Not the primary centre of the Kajari Mahotsav.

 

• Kushi Nagar (Option 3): Known for Buddhist heritage (Mahaparinirvana site of Buddha), not for the Kajari Mahotsav.

 

• Jhansi (Option 4): Known for the Rani Lakshmibai fort and history, not for the Kajari Mahotsav.

question: Matki dance is the famous folk dance associated with which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Matki dance is a famous folk dance of Madhya Pradesh, particularly from the Malwa region, in which women dance while balancing an earthen pot (matki) on their heads. (मटकी नृत्य — मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• It is traditionally performed to celebrate the joy of good harvests and various festive occasions in rural Malwa, showcasing balance and grace.

 

• The dance is often accompanied by folk songs and traditional instruments and is closely tied to the Kalbelia-adjacent tribal and rural culture of central India.

 

• Madhya Pradesh is also home to other tribal dance forms such as Gaur, Karma, Saila and Dandar, performed by communities like the Gonds and Baigas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhil, Gond, Korku and Baiga are among the major tribal communities of Madhya Pradesh known for their distinctive dance and art traditions.

 

• Madhya Pradesh's tribal art also includes the famous Gond painting tradition.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 1): Known for Bhangra and Giddha, not Matki dance.

 

• Gujarat (Option 2): Known for Garba and Dandiya Raas, not Matki dance.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 4): Known for Lavani and Tamasha, not Matki dance.

question: Which of the following is a species of tropical deciduous forests?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Teak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Teak (Tectona grandis) is the classic and most economically important species of India's tropical deciduous (monsoon) forests, which shed their leaves during the dry season. (सागौन — उष्णकटिबंधीय पर्णपाती वन)

 

• Tropical deciduous forests are further classified into moist deciduous (rainfall 100-200 cm, e.g. teak, sal, shisham) and dry deciduous (rainfall 70-100 cm, e.g. teak, tendu, khair) types in India.

 

• Teak is prized for its durable, water-resistant timber, used extensively in furniture and shipbuilding, and is found widely in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Kerala.

 

• Other important species of India's deciduous forests include Sal, Sheesham, Sandalwood and Khair.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sal (Shorea robusta) dominates the moist deciduous forests of the eastern and central Indian states like Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Odisha.

 

• Tropical evergreen forests, by contrast, are found in areas with over 200 cm rainfall, such as the Western Ghats and Northeast India.

 

NOTE

 

• Palms (Option 1): Characteristic of tropical evergreen/rainforests, not deciduous forests.

 

• Mahogany (Option 2): Associated with tropical evergreen forests, valued for fine furniture wood.

 

• Ebony (Option 4): Associated with tropical evergreen forests, not deciduous forests.

question: Which Lavani singer got Padma Shri 2022 by the President of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sulochana Chavan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sulochana Chavan, popularly known as the ‘Lavani Queen (Lavani Samragyi)’, was conferred the Padma Shri in 2022 by President Ram Nath Kovind, in recognition of her contribution to Lavani folk singing of Maharashtra. (सुलोचना चव्हाण — पद्म श्री 2022, लावणी गायिका)

 

• She was celebrated for her signature fast-paced singing style known as ‘jhatka-style’ or fast-tempo Lavani, and had a career spanning over six decades, including playback singing for Marathi films.

 

• Sulochana Chavan passed away in December 2022 at the age of 92, shortly after receiving this honour.

 

• The Padma Shri is India's fourth-highest civilian award, conferred annually by the President of India on the recommendation of the Padma Awards Committee.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lavani is a traditional folk performance combining song and dance, popular in Maharashtra, often performed in the Tamasha theatre tradition.

 

• Other notable Marathi playback and folk singers include Asha Bhosle, who is also closely associated with Lavani-style songs in Hindi and Marathi cinema.

 

NOTE

 

• Bela Shende (Option 2): A well-known Marathi/Hindi playback singer, but not the recipient of the Padma Shri 2022 for Lavani.

 

• Vaishali Samant (Option 3): A noted Marathi playback singer, but not this particular Padma Shri 2022 awardee.

 

• Devaki Pandit (Option 4): A noted classical/playback singer, but not the Padma Shri 2022 awardee for Lavani.

question: Which of the following is the most acidic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is HCOOH.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• HCOOH (formic acid/methanoic acid) is the most acidic among the given carboxylic acids because it has no alkyl group attached to the carboxyl group. (फॉर्मिक अम्ल — सबसे अधिक अम्लीय)

 

• Alkyl groups (like CH3-, C2H5-, C3H7-) are electron-donating (+I effect), which reduces the polarity of the O-H bond and destabilises the conjugate base, thereby decreasing acidity as the alkyl chain gets longer/bulkier.

 

• Since HCOOH has a hydrogen atom instead of an alkyl group attached to -COOH, it lacks this electron-donating effect, making its O-H bond more polar and easier to ionise — hence it is the strongest acid of the four.

 

• The order of acidic strength among these acids is: HCOOH > CH3COOH > C2H5COOH > C3H7COOH, i.e. acidity decreases as the alkyl chain length increases.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Formic acid is naturally found in the stings of ants and bees and is used industrially in leather tanning, textile dyeing and as a preservative.

 

• The pKa of formic acid (~3.75) is lower than that of acetic acid (~4.76), confirming it is the stronger acid.

 

NOTE

 

• C2H5COOH (Option 2): Propanoic acid; weaker than formic and acetic acid due to a longer electron-donating alkyl chain.

 

• C3H7COOH (Option 3): Butanoic acid; the weakest acid among the four due to the longest alkyl chain and strongest +I effect.

 

• CH3COOH (Option 4): Acetic acid; more acidic than propanoic/butanoic acid but weaker than formic acid, which has no alkyl group at all.

question: The Maukharis ruled over which of the following cities in western Uttar Pradesh that over the time replaced Pataliputra as a political centre of north India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kannauj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Maukhari dynasty ruled from Kannauj (Kanyakubja), which gradually emerged as the leading political centre of North India in the post-Gupta period, replacing the earlier Magadhan capital Pataliputra. (मौखरि वंश — कन्नौज)

 

• The Maukharis rose from feudatory status under the Guptas to become an independent power centred on Kannauj by the 6th century CE.

 

• Kannauj subsequently became the capital of Harshavardhana's empire in the 7th century, and later the object of the prolonged ‘Tripartite Struggle’ between the Palas, Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas.

 

• Its strategic location in the fertile Ganga-Yamuna Doab of western Uttar Pradesh made it an important centre of trade, culture and political power for several centuries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pataliputra (modern Patna) had earlier been the capital of the Mauryas, Shungas and Guptas.

 

• The Gurjara-Pratiharas eventually held Kannauj as their capital for the longest period during the Tripartite Struggle.

 

NOTE

 

• Bareli (Option 2): A city in western Uttar Pradesh, but not the Maukhari capital.

 

• Agra (Option 3): Rose to prominence much later, mainly under the Mughals, not associated with the Maukharis.

 

• Kanpur (Option 4): An important modern industrial city, but not the historic Maukhari capital.

question: Which of the following is NOT a greenhouse gas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nitric oxide.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nitric oxide (NO) is not classified as a greenhouse gas; it is a short-lived, reactive free radical involved in atmospheric chemistry (e.g. ozone layer reactions) rather than in trapping long-wave radiation like true greenhouse gases. (नाइट्रिक ऑक्साइड — ग्रीनहाउस गैस नहीं)

 

• The major greenhouse gases recognised under the Kyoto Protocol/UNFCCC are Carbon dioxide (CO2), Methane (CH4), Nitrous oxide (N2O), Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), Perfluorocarbons (PFCs), Sulphur hexafluoride (SF6) and Nitrogen trifluoride (NF3).

 

• Water vapour is also a very significant, naturally occurring greenhouse gas, though it is not included in emissions treaties as it isn't directly emitted by human activity in the same way.

 

• Greenhouse gases trap infrared (long-wave) radiation reflected from the Earth's surface, causing the greenhouse effect and global warming; NO does not have this significant heat-trapping role in the lower atmosphere.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nitrous oxide (N2O), not to be confused with nitric oxide, is a potent greenhouse gas mainly from agricultural and industrial sources, with a global warming potential much higher than CO2.

 

• Methane has a much higher global warming potential than CO2 over a 20-year period, though it persists in the atmosphere for a shorter time.

 

NOTE

 

• Methane (Option 1): A recognised greenhouse gas, emitted from livestock, wetlands and fossil fuel extraction.

 

• Carbon dioxide (Option 2): The most abundant anthropogenic greenhouse gas, mainly from fossil fuel combustion.

 

• Nitrous oxide (Option 3): A recognised greenhouse gas under the Kyoto Protocol, mainly from agriculture and industry.

question: Which allotrope of carbon was discovered by Robert F Curl, Harold W Kroto and Richard E Smalley in 1985?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fullerene.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fullerene (specifically Buckminsterfullerene, C60) was discovered in 1985 by Robert F. Curl, Sir Harold W. Kroto and Richard E. Smalley, for which they jointly won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1996. (फुलरीन — कार्बन का अपररूप, 1985)

 

• Fullerene molecules are cage-like, closed structures made entirely of carbon atoms arranged in a pattern of hexagons and pentagons, resembling a soccer ball in the case of C60.

 

• It is one of the several known allotropes of carbon, alongside diamond, graphite, graphene and carbon nanotubes.

 

• Fullerenes have applications in nanotechnology, drug delivery, materials science and superconductivity research due to their unique cage structure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Graphene, a single layer of graphite's hexagonal carbon lattice, was isolated much later, in 2004, by Andre Geim and Konstantin Novoselov (Nobel Prize 2010).

 

• Diamond and graphite are the classical, naturally occurring allotropes of carbon, differing in their bonding structure (sp3 vs sp2).

 

NOTE

 

• Graphene (Option 1): Isolated in 2004 by Geim and Novoselov, not discovered by Curl, Kroto and Smalley in 1985.

 

• Lonsdaleite (Option 2): A rare hexagonal form of diamond, first identified from meteorite impact sites in 1967, unrelated to this 1985 discovery.

 

• Carbophene (Option 3): Not a recognised/established allotrope of carbon; a distractor option.

question: Annapurna Devi is associated with which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Surbahar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Annapurna Devi was a renowned Indian classical musician associated with the Surbahar (bass sitar), belonging to the Maihar gharana. (अन्नपूर्णा देवी — सुरबहार)

 

• She was the daughter of the legendary Ustad Allauddin Khan and the first wife of Pandit Ravi Shankar; she was also the elder sister of Ustad Ali Akbar Khan (sarod maestro).

 

• Despite retreating from public performances for much of her life, she was widely regarded by peers as one of the greatest instrumentalists of her generation, and trained several notable disciples including Hariprasad Chaurasia and Nikhil Banerjee.

 

• She was honoured with the Padma Bhushan in 1977 (which she famously declined) and later the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Surbahar is a large, deep-toned plucked string instrument, often described as the bass version of the sitar, particularly suited to playing dhrupad-style alap.

 

• The Maihar gharana, founded by Ustad Allauddin Khan, produced several legendary musicians including Ravi Shankar (sitar) and Ali Akbar Khan (sarod).

 

NOTE

 

• Rudra veena (Option 1): A different, ancient stick-zither instrument used in dhrupad music, not Annapurna Devi's primary instrument.

 

• Taal (Option 2): Refers to rhythmic cycles in Indian classical music, not a musical instrument itself.

 

• Ektara (Option 3): A simple one-stringed folk instrument, unrelated to Annapurna Devi.

question: Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India lays down that ‘The allocation of seats in the Council of States to be filled by representatives of the States and of the Union territories shall be in accordance with the provisions in that behalf contained in the fourth Schedule’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 80.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 80 of the Constitution of India deals with the composition of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha), and its clause (2) contains this exact provision regarding allocation of seats as per the Fourth Schedule. (अनुच्छेद 80 — राज्यसभा की संरचना, चतुर्थ अनुसूची)

 

• As per Article 80, the Rajya Sabha can have a maximum of 250 members — up to 238 elected representatives of States/UTs and 12 members nominated by the President for their special knowledge in fields like literature, science, art and social service.

 

• The Fourth Schedule of the Constitution specifically lays down the number of seats allotted to each State and Union Territory in the Rajya Sabha.

 

• Members representing States in the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies through the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 81 deals with the composition of the Lok Sabha (House of the People).

 

• Article 83 deals with the duration of the Houses of Parliament, while Article 82 relates to readjustment after each Census.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 81 (Option 1): Deals with the composition of the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha's seat allocation via the Fourth Schedule.

 

• Article 82 (Option 2): Deals with readjustment of seats after each Census.

 

• Article 83 (Option 3): Deals with the duration of Parliament's Houses.

question: In the year 1925, who extracted lipids from an erythrocyte sample and found that lipid monolayers are good for measuring molecular surface area versus lateral pressure?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gorter and Grendel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In 1925, Evert Gorter and Francois Grendel extracted lipids from red blood cell (erythrocyte) membranes and, by spreading them as a monolayer on water, calculated that the surface area of the lipid layer was about twice the surface area of the cells — leading them to propose the lipid bilayer model of the cell membrane. (गॉर्टर और ग्रेंडेल — लिपिड द्विस्तर मॉडल, 1925)

 

• Their experiment used the Langmuir trough technique to measure how lipid molecules behave as monolayers, relating molecular surface area to lateral (surface) pressure.

 

• This pioneering work laid the foundation for the later fluid mosaic model of the cell membrane, proposed by S.J. Singer and Garth Nicolson in 1972.

 

• The Gorter-Grendel experiment is considered one of the earliest pieces of experimental evidence for the existence of a lipid bilayer in biological membranes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The fluid mosaic model (1972) describes the cell membrane as a dynamic structure with proteins embedded in/on a fluid lipid bilayer.

 

• Robertson's unit membrane model (1959) was another important intermediate step in membrane structure studies, based on electron microscopy.

 

NOTE

 

• Carson and Eccles (Option 2): Not associated with this 1925 erythrocyte lipid monolayer experiment; a distractor pairing.

 

• Avery and Buck (Option 3): Not associated with this experiment; Avery is more famously linked (with MacLeod and McCarty) to identifying DNA as genetic material.

 

• Margulis and Ruska (Option 4): Not associated with this experiment; Lynn Margulis is known for the endosymbiotic theory, and Ernst Ruska for developing the electron microscope.

question:
Identify the sequence of implementation of the following taxes.

I. Land revenue

II. Sales tax

III. MODVAT

IV. Service tax
solution_text:
The correct answer is I, II, III, IV.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct chronological sequence of implementation is: Land revenue → Sales tax → MODVAT → Service tax, i.e. I, II, III, IV. (भूमि राजस्व, बिक्री कर, मोडवैट, सेवा कर — कालानुक्रम)

 

• Land revenue is the oldest of these levies, tracing back to ancient and medieval Indian administration and continuing through British colonial rule (e.g. the Permanent Settlement of 1793).

 

• Sales tax on the sale of goods was introduced by various Indian states starting in the late 1930s (Madras Presidency introduced it first, in 1939), well before independence-era indirect tax reforms.

 

• MODVAT (Modified Value Added Tax), a scheme allowing manufacturers credit for excise duty paid on inputs, was introduced in 1986, while Service Tax was introduced later, in 1994, under the Finance Act.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• MODVAT was later renamed CENVAT (Central Value Added Tax) in the year 2000.

 

• Both Sales tax and Service tax were eventually subsumed into the Goods and Services Tax (GST), implemented in India from 1 July 2017.

 

NOTE

 

• III, II, IV, I (Option 1): Places MODVAT (1986) before Sales tax and Land revenue, which is chronologically incorrect.

 

• II, IV, I, III (Option 2): Places Sales tax and Service tax before Land revenue, which is chronologically incorrect since land revenue is the oldest of the four.

 

• IV, II, I, III (Option 3): Places Service tax (1994) first and Land revenue third, which is chronologically incorrect.

question: Under which of the following Pala king's patronage the Vikramshila university in 8th century India was founded?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dharmapala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vikramshila University was founded in the late 8th century CE by Dharmapala, the second ruler of the Pala dynasty, in present-day Bhagalpur district, Bihar. (विक्रमशिला विश्वविद्यालय — धर्मपाल, पाल वंश)

 

• Along with Nalanda, Vikramshila became one of the most important centres of Buddhist learning, especially renowned for Vajrayana (Tantric) Buddhism.

 

• Dharmapala was also the founder of the great monastery at Somapura (Paharpur, present-day Bangladesh) and greatly expanded Pala power across eastern India.

 

• Vikramshila continued to flourish for several centuries until it was destroyed by the forces of Bakhtiyar Khilji around the early 13th century, similar to the fate of Nalanda.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gopala, Dharmapala's father, was the founder of the Pala dynasty, elected by the region's chiefs to end the political anarchy known as ‘Matsyanyaya’ in Bengal.

 

• Devapala, Dharmapala's son and successor, further expanded the Pala Empire and continued strong patronage of Buddhist institutions.

 

NOTE

 

• Gopala (Option 1): He was the founder of the Pala dynasty, not the founder of Vikramshila University.

 

• Mahipala I (Option 2): A later Pala king (10th-11th century) known for reviving Pala power, but not the founder of Vikramshila.

 

• Devapala (Option 3): Dharmapala's successor, who continued patronage of Buddhist learning but did not found Vikramshila University.

question: What is the amount of financial assistance provided per month to girl students studying in government schools under the ‘Tamil Nadu Pudhumai Penn Scheme’ launched by the Government of Tamil Nadu in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is ₹1,000 per month.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tamil Nadu Pudhumai Penn Scheme, launched by the Government of Tamil Nadu in 2021-2023, provides a monthly financial assistance of ₹1,000 directly to the bank accounts of eligible girl students. (पुधुमई पेन योजना — तमिलनाडु, ₹1,000 प्रति माह)

 

• The scheme is aimed at girl students studying in government and government-aided schools, from Class 11 up to the completion of their undergraduate degree, to prevent dropouts and encourage higher education.

 

• The financial assistance amounts to ₹12,000 per year, transferred directly under a Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism to the student's own bank account.

 

• The scheme is implemented by the Tamil Nadu Department of Social Welfare and Women Empowerment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The scheme's name ‘Pudhumai Penn’ translates to ‘New Woman’ in Tamil, reflecting its aim of women's empowerment through education.

 

• Tamil Nadu has several other welfare schemes for girls, including the older ‘Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Ninaivu Marriage Assistance Scheme’.

 

NOTE

 

• ₹500 per month (Option 1): Understates the actual monthly assistance amount under this scheme.

 

• ₹3,000 per month (Option 2): Overstates the actual monthly assistance amount under this scheme.

 

• ₹2,000 per month (Option 4): Overstates the actual monthly assistance amount under this scheme.

question: Under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, the maximum premium payable by the farmers will be _________ for all kharif food and oilseeds crops.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), launched in 2016, the maximum premium payable by farmers for all Kharif food and oilseed crops is 2% of the sum insured (or the actuarial premium rate, whichever is lower). (प्रधानमंत्री फसल बीमा योजना — खरीफ फसलें, 2% प्रीमियम)

 

• For Rabi food and oilseed crops, the maximum premium payable by farmers is 1.5% of the sum insured.

 

• For annual commercial and horticultural crops, the maximum premium payable is 5% of the sum insured.

 

• The remaining actual premium amount, after the farmer's share, is subsidised and shared equally between the Central and State Governments (with variations for certain states/UTs).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• PMFBY is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and aims to provide comprehensive crop insurance coverage against yield losses due to natural calamities, pests and diseases.

 

• The scheme uses technology such as satellite imagery, drones and smartphones for quick and accurate yield estimation.

 

NOTE

 

• 4% (Option 1): Not the applicable premium rate for kharif crops under PMFBY.

 

• 6% (Option 3): Not the applicable premium rate for kharif crops under PMFBY.

 

• 8% (Option 4): Not the applicable premium rate for kharif crops under PMFBY.

question: What is the primary objective of the 'Standup India' initiative?
option_3: To facilitate bank loans for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs
option_4: To support all types of startups
solution_text:
The correct answer is To facilitate bank loans for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Stand-Up India Scheme, launched on 5 April 2016, primarily aims to facilitate bank loans between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore to at least one Scheduled Caste (SC) or Scheduled Tribe (ST) borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch, for setting up greenfield enterprises. (स्टैंड-अप इंडिया — SC/ST और महिला उद्यमियों हेतु ऋण)

 

• The scheme is aimed at promoting entrepreneurship among under-represented groups by easing access to institutional credit for setting up new businesses in manufacturing, services, trading or the agri-allied sector.

 

• It is implemented through scheduled commercial bank branches, with support from the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) via the Stand-Up India portal.

 

• The scheme complements the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana, which focuses on smaller loans for micro-enterprises across all social categories.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Stand-Up India was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, alongside other flagship schemes like Startup India and Make in India.

 

• The scheme also provides hand-holding support covering pre-loan training, facilitation and factoring.

 

NOTE

 

• To boost the manufacturing sector (Option 1): This describes the objective of schemes like ‘Make in India’, not Stand-Up India specifically.

 

• To promote digital transactions nationwide (Option 2): This describes objectives of schemes like Digital India/BHIM, not Stand-Up India.

 

• To support all types of startups (Option 4): This more broadly describes the ‘Startup India’ initiative, whereas Stand-Up India is specifically targeted at SC/ST and women entrepreneurs.

question: Which fundamental duty applies on you when you see a few school students, on their educational trip to Humayun’s tomb, writing their names on the walls?
option_2: To defend the country and render national service
option_3: To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
option_4: To protect and improve the natural environment
solution_text:
The correct answer is To safeguard public property.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 51A(i) of the Indian Constitution, it is a fundamental duty of every citizen ‘to safeguard public property and to abjure violence’. (सार्वजनिक संपत्ति की रक्षा — मौलिक कर्तव्य, अनुच्छेद 51A(i))

 

• Humayun's Tomb, a UNESCO World Heritage monument in Delhi, is a piece of public/national heritage property; defacing its walls by writing names on them amounts to damaging public property.

 

• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, and are listed under Part IVA.

 

• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties, applicable to all citizens of India, though they are non-justiciable (not directly enforceable by courts).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 11th Fundamental Duty, added later by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, relates to providing opportunities for education to children between ages 6-14.

 

• Fundamental Duties were inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Soviet Union).

 

NOTE

 

• To defend the country and render national service (Option 2): This is a separate duty under Article 51A(d), unrelated to defacing monuments.

 

• To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India (Option 3): This is a separate duty under Article 51A(c), not the one relevant to damaging heritage property.

 

• To protect and improve the natural environment (Option 4): This duty under Article 51A(g) relates to forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, not built heritage monuments.

question: In the second Round Table Conference, Mahatma Gandhi represented which of the following parties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian National Congress.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mahatma Gandhi attended the Second Round Table Conference (1931) in London as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress, following the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of March 1931. (द्वितीय गोलमेज सम्मेलन — महात्मा गांधी, भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस)

 

• The Second Round Table Conference was held from September to December 1931, and Gandhi's participation followed the suspension of the Civil Disobedience Movement under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

 

• The conference largely failed due to disagreements over the issue of separate electorates for minorities and depressed classes, particularly Gandhi's opposition to B.R. Ambedkar's demand on this matter.

 

• On returning to India, Gandhi resumed the Civil Disobedience Movement in January 1932 after the talks proved fruitless.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The First Round Table Conference (1930-31) was boycotted by the Indian National Congress, whose leaders were in jail at the time.

 

• The Third Round Table Conference (1932) was also boycotted by the Congress, with only a small number of Indian delegates attending overall.

 

NOTE

 

• Communist Party of India (Option 1): Not the party Gandhi represented; the CPI was not part of the official Congress delegation.

 

• All India Forward Bloc (Option 3): This party was founded later, in 1939, by Subhas Chandra Bose, well after the Round Table Conferences.

 

• Muslim League (Option 4): A separate party represented by its own leaders (like Muhammad Ali Jinnah), not by Gandhi.

question: Through which routes is the majority of India’s international trade carried out?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sea and air.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The majority of India's international trade, by both volume and value, is carried out via sea and air routes, since these connect India to its global trading partners across oceans and continents. (भारत का अंतर्राष्ट्रीय व्यापार — समुद्री एवं वायु मार्ग)

 

• Sea routes handle the bulk of trade by volume (bulky, low-value cargo such as ores, coal, petroleum and grains), transported via India's major and minor ports.

 

• Air routes handle a significant share of trade by value, especially for high-value, low-bulk, time-sensitive goods such as electronics, gems and jewellery, and perishables.

 

• India has 12 major ports and over 200 minor/intermediate ports, along with international airports like Mumbai, Delhi and Chennai, that together handle the overwhelming share of the country's foreign trade.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Railways, while important for domestic trade, cannot serve most of India's international trade due to the absence of continuous rail links with most trading partners (barring limited routes to neighbouring countries like Nepal and Bangladesh).

 

• The Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Mumbai) is India's largest container port, handling a substantial share of the country's containerised sea trade.

 

NOTE

 

• Railway and air (Option 1): Railways play a negligible role in India's overall international trade; sea, not rail, dominates alongside air.

 

• Only Railway (Option 3): Incorrect, as railways handle only a minimal share of international trade, largely limited to a few neighbouring countries.

 

• Sea and railway (Option 4): Railways are not a major mode for India's international trade; air, not rail, is the second major mode alongside sea.

question: Which of the following options indicates the size of PPLO (Pleuro Pneumonia Like Organisms)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is About 0.1 µm.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• PPLO (Pleuro Pneumonia Like Organisms), now classified as Mycoplasma, are among the smallest known free-living/cellular organisms, with a size of about 0.1 µm (100 nanometres). (पीपीएलओ/माइकोप्लाज्मा — सबसे छोटे स्वतंत्र-जीवी जीव)

 

• Mycoplasma organisms lack a rigid cell wall, which allows them to assume varied and irregular shapes and pass through most bacteria-retaining filters.

 

• They were originally named PPLO after their resemblance to the organism causing contagious bovine pleuropneumonia, before being reclassified under the genus Mycoplasma.

 

• Some species of Mycoplasma are pathogenic, causing diseases in humans, animals and plants (e.g. Mycoplasma pneumoniae, a cause of atypical pneumonia in humans).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mycoplasma are notable in biology as organisms that blur the line between viruses and typical bacteria due to their minute size, though they are true cells with both DNA and RNA, unlike viruses.

 

• Their genome is among the smallest of any known free-living organism, making them a model system for minimal-genome studies (e.g. Craig Venter's synthetic biology work).

 

NOTE

 

• About 30 µm (Option 1): Far larger than the actual size of PPLO/Mycoplasma.

 

• About 20 µm (Option 2): Far larger than the actual size of PPLO/Mycoplasma.

 

• About 10 µm (Option 4): Larger than the actual size of PPLO/Mycoplasma.
